rationale: This is PayoutStrainExternallyFunded with the accrual leg swapped for the archive's BookTaxGapFinancedGrowth accrual leg — a mechanical recombination of two already-tested triples rather than a new mechanism, and the third rank multiplication further dilutes an already thin (0.084) sample.

Identically a cosmetic swap: CleanSurplusFundedWCBloat multiplied by the same payout-strain rank already tested in PayoutStrainExternallyFunded, so the only genuinely new information is a coverage difference, which does not justify a generation.

The debt-maturity-composition leg is a genuinely distinct financing-pressure channel (no quantity-of-capital-raised leg in the archive captures it), the expression matches the hypothesis and the sign direction is unambiguous, and coverage should be high; the main residual risk is that short-term debt share shifts partly reflect firm size/credit quality rather than rollover strain.

The long-lived-asset side of accounting quality is a legitimate gap in the archive (and DEPI-style depreciation-rate declines are a recognized manipulation flag), but Δ(dp/at) falls mechanically when the asset base grows fast, which is exactly what the externally-financed-growth leg measures, so the interaction is largely asset-growth squared and any result will not identify the stated expense-recognition mechanism.

The `ib` terms cancel algebraically — the bracket reduces to (Δdebt + Δceq + dvc − oancf)/at — so despite the hypothesis the signal contains no accrual/earnings-quality content at all, and dvc enters both the level and the strain weight, double-counting the payout term.

Decomposing the netted working-capital accrual into asset-build and payable-stretch sides is a substantive re-specification rather than a re-weighting and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the liability leg bets against the documented direction of the accrual anomaly (payables growth lowers accruals and predicts higher returns) on thin justification, and the three-way rank product will diffuse whatever spread survives.
